verifications.claim: id: PAT_AKHANNOUCH; nameMain: Akhannouch; nameSystem: hereditary_family_name; transmissionMode: other; designatedSocialUnit: lineage

candidates.title: Vidéo. À Aguerd Oudad, le fief des Akhannouch
candidates.author: M'hand Oubarka
candidates.quote: L'Haj Hmad Akhannouch, patriarche de cette famille aujourd'hui prospère, en est originaire.
candidates.supports: Attests Akhannouch as a family name tied to the douar of Aguerd Oudad near Tafraout (Souss, Morocco). Says nothing about meaning or the PPL_CHLEUH link, which stays unsupported.

verifications.claim: id: PAT_ALAO; nameMain: Alao; nameSystem: praise_name; transmissionMode: other; designatedSocialUnit: other

candidates.title: Àlàó - YorubaNames
candidates.quote: One destined to divide and conquer his/her enemies. [...] à-là-wó [...] A cognomen, oríkì.
candidates.supports: Classes Alao as an oriki (praise name), gives the morphology and a gloss, and lists Arisekola Alao (1945-2014, Ibadan politician and businessman). Collaborative dictionary: community tier at best. Says nothing about Benin (BEN), so the country claim is not supported by it.

verifications.claim: id: PAT_ALAOUI; nameMain: Alaoui; nameSystem: nisba; transmissionMode: other; designatedSocialUnit: lineage

candidates.title: « Si Mohammed! » : Names as Address Forms in Moroccan Arabic
candidates.quote: Traditional family names may derive from prestigious Andalusian Muslim families (Benchekroun, Bennani), Arab tribes (al-Fihri, as-Sufyani) or Arab dynasties (al-Alaoui, al-Idrissi), or place names
candidates.supports: Shows that al-Alaoui is a Moroccan family name of dynastic origin, consistent with the nisba classification. Read in this session from the downloaded PDF; author not checked on the PDF.

verifications.claim: id: PAT_AL_DANAGLA; nameMain: al-Danagla; nameSystem: nisba; transmissionMode: other; designatedSocialUnit: other

candidates.title: A History of the Arabs in the Sudan, vol. I
candidates.author: Harold Alfred MacMichael
candidates.quote: commonly known to the south as Danagla, i.e. inhabitants of Dongola
candidates.supports: Danagla as a group name meaning 'inhabitants of Dongola' (p. 13, colonial-era source, to be labelled as such). Read in the Internet Archive full text.
